requirements.name: Calm first screen
requirements.why: Oct 3 round 2 and the calm-UI rule: the first screen must answer “is it OK, what needs me?” before anything else, with colour only for exceptions.
requirements.pass: At 1440 × 900 the needs-you and stalled tracks are visible and readable as words without scrolling; ordinary tracks read grey.

anchors.1: Needs-you is buried or only a raw number signals trouble.
anchors.3: Needs-you is on screen but competes with equal-weight detail.
anchors.5: Needs-you and stalled lead the screen; everything else is quiet.

requirements.name: Reuses agent-UI muscle memory
requirements.why: His brief: lean on the Claude Code / Codex sidebar he already uses all day — collapsible project groups, + New, grouped by folder.
requirements.pass: The drill-in panel behaves like the Claude desktop / Codex project tree (collapse, select, new project with 1..N folders).

anchors.3: A tree exists but with different semantics or only partly.
anchors.5: The same tree, the same gestures, where he expects them.

requirements.name: Scales to 10 projects × 5 tracks
requirements.why: Six projects today; the board must not fall apart at ten, with multi-folder projects and dozens of sessions.
requirements.pass: With the 10-project fixture he can still see what needs him and reach any track in two clicks.

anchors.3: Works, with long scrolls or hidden needs-you.
anchors.5: Collapse / grouping keep it to about one screen and needs-you stays findable.

requirements.name: File-first fit
requirements.why: Vibe Tracks is file-first: a project is a .vibetrack file listing roots, a track is a file, the evaluator writes KPI rows.
requirements.pass: Every element on the first screen derives from today's files (project file, track files, KPI ledgers) without a new hand-kept store.

anchors.1: Needs a new database or hand-kept state.
anchors.3: Its core structure leans on an unbuilt join.
anchors.5: Everything derives from files that exist or are one field away.

requirements.name: Cost to build on the Dashboard lane
requirements.why: The Dashboard lane (vibetracks-dashboard, Variant A: TracksPage + TrackPage inside Clank) is where this lands; less rewrite = sooner in his hands.
requirements.pass: The variant extends Variant A's L1 table and L2 track page rather than replacing them, and does not fight Clank's own left panel.

anchors.1: A new shell that fights Clank.
anchors.3: New component families beside Variant A.
anchors.5: Extends Variant A's table and page with a small new panel.

gates.name: Every brief element works by real clicks
gates.why: rows ↔ board, project highlight + filter, collapse, project page, track page, left panel on drill-in, New-project dialog (name + 1..N folders) — driven by Playwright clicks, read back from the DOM.

gates.name: No sideways page scroll at 390 px
gates.why: Home, board, project and track pages measured at 390 × 844 and 1440 × 900 (document and main scroller).

gates.name: Calm state words lead
gates.why: Each track shows On track / Stalled / Needs you / Holding as a word; a raw number is never the only signal.

gates.name: Zach's Oct 6 feedback is in every variant
gates.why: Several soft KPIs per track (summary = row sparkline; small multiples on the track page) with hard gates kept separate · Done and Archived as board states you can drag into · project north star (lagging) above its tracks' KPIs (leading) · Auditor panel + row badge · evo-style Experiments tree tied to roadmap rungs · Discover vs Optimize modes. Checked by Playwright clicks and a real drag.

variants.name: Calm Rows
variants.thesis: Home is one full-width list of track rows under collapsible project summary strips; the Claude-style sidebar appears only once you drill in.

axes.Project header: one-line strip: rollup · north star · spark · agents
axes.Board columns: health: Needs you · Stalled · On track · Done · Archived
axes.Track page: tabs, opens on Overview (KPIs, gates, roadmap)

decisions: Home stays the full-width ledger the brief asked for; no panel steals width on the overview.
Project header row carries the rollup words, the north star and its sparkline, and a live-agent count.
Board columns are health (Needs you · Stalled · On track · Holding), so the board is the same question as home, sorted.
Drill-in brings the Claude desktop tree: projects → tracks, status dot, live-agent count.
variants.bestWhen: He wants the overview calm and wide, and drills in to work.
variants.losesWhen: At 10+ projects a needs-you row can sit below the fold unless its project is expanded near the top.

variants.name: Codex Shell
variants.thesis: The Codex / Claude desktop shell unchanged: a permanent left tree of projects → tracks on every page, home included, with live-agent counts as sidebar badges.

axes.Sidebar: always (home too), with Home / Board nav

decisions: The sidebar never disappears, so position in the tree is always visible.
Board columns are the track's mode (Discover · Optimize) plus Done and Archived — evo's discover / optimise split as the board's question; dragging a card between them flips its mode.
Rows drop the session chips; the sidebar badge says who is on it.
variants.bestWhen: He lives in the Codex / Claude app all day and wants zero relearning.
variants.losesWhen: Inside Clank there are now two left panels (Clank's file tree + this), and home shows every track twice.

variants.name: Ledger Table
variants.thesis: Home is one dense, sortable table (Linear list view) with project group rows and a Group-by switch; drill-in keeps a 52 px monogram rail that opens on hover.

axes.Sidebar: 52 px rail on drill-in, hover or pin to open
axes.Board columns: state × project grid (5 states incl. Done, Archived)
axes.Track page: one dense page: KPIs, gates, roadmap, auditor, sessions, experiments, no tabs

decisions: Group by Project / State / None; sort by state, name or agents.
The board is a grid: projects as swimlanes, health as columns.
The rail keeps the page wide and still marks needs-you / stalled per project with a corner dot.
variants.bestWhen: Tracks grow past ~30 and he wants to scan, sort and compare.
variants.losesWhen: The first screen is nine columns of equal-weight cells — the opposite of calm.

variants.name: Project Boards
variants.thesis: Each project is its own mini-dashboard on home: a big north-star chart on the left, its track rows on the right; the board makes every project a column.

axes.Sidebar: on drill-in, with a north-star spark per project
axes.Project header: mini-dashboard with a big north-star chart
axes.Board columns: projects, each with Done and Archived shelves
axes.Live agents: chips on rows + count under the chart

decisions: The north star is the biggest thing on the page, per project.
A collapsed card keeps its north star and spark in the header.
Board columns are projects, so highlight is mostly redundant.
variants.bestWhen: Projects, not tracks, are the unit he reviews (a weekly business review per project).
variants.losesWhen: Only one and a half projects fit above the fold, and ten project columns overflow the board.
keep: north-star chart on the project page

variants.name: Live Ops
variants.thesis: Home answers “what needs me” in a band above the rows and shows every live agent in a right rail; drill-in shows the Claude sidebar literally — chats as leaves under their track.

axes.Sidebar: on drill-in, with chat leaves under each track
axes.Board columns: who moves next: You · An agent · Nobody · Done · Archived
axes.Live agents: right rail grouped by project, and sidebar leaves

decisions: Needs-you and stalled lift out of the list into a band with the action (Answer · Start agent).
The board asks “whose move is it?”, not “how healthy is it?”.
Sessions are first-class leaves under tracks — the Oct 6 session ↔ track join made visible.
variants.bestWhen: Most of his day is unblocking agents across accounts.
variants.losesWhen: The session ↔ track join only covers 18 % of KPI rows today, and at scale the leaves and the rail get long.

fr1: Summary sentence + the one needs-you and one stalled row as words above the fold; everything else grey (v1-home).
fr2: Drill-in tree is the Claude desktop tree (collapse, status dots, live counts, + New project); home deliberately has no sidebar, unlike the Claude app.
fr3: 10-project fixture: all ten projects collapse to one screen with rollup words still flagging needs-you; expanded it is 3.1 screens and 1 of 2 needs-you tracks sits below the fold.
fr4: Strip = project file (name, roots) + north-star KPI; rows = track files + latest KPI row; chips degrade to “no agent” without the join.
fr5: Variant A's TracksPage is already one row per track; project group rows + a drill-in panel are additive. Board and dialog are new.

fr1: Same summary sentence and needs row, but a 268 px tree repeats every track beside the list on the first screen.
fr2: Identical to the Codex / Claude shell: permanent tree, Home / Board / New project at its top, live badges.
fr3: 3.1 screens expanded, 1 of 2 needs-you tracks above the fold; the tree collapses per project and synthetic projects start collapsed.
fr4: Same data as V1; the board's mode columns read the track file's vibe-mode, Done / Archived its vibe-status.
fr5: A permanent plugin sidebar sits next to Clank's own left panel on every page and narrows Variant A's table everywhere.

fr1: Needs-you is one orange row among ten equal-weight columns, and the track page stacks KPIs, auditor, sessions and experiments on one page; scanning is fast, calm is not.
fr2: The rail is closer to VS Code's activity bar than the Claude sidebar; the full tree is one hover away.
fr3: Densest at scale: 2.7 screens expanded; Group by State puts both needs-you tracks first in one click (grouped by project, 1 of 2 is above the fold).
fr4: Pure projection of track files + KPI rows.
fr5: Closest to Variant A's fixed-layout table; the rail and swimlane grid are new but small.

fr1: Needs-you is inside the first card; other projects' trouble starts below the fold (only ~1.5 projects visible).
fr2: Sidebar on drill-in matches; the home cards are a dashboard idiom, not an agent-UI one.
fr3: 3.8 screens expanded; ten project columns overflow the board by 966 px sideways at 1440 (scrolls inside the board).
fr4: Needs a north-star series per project at chart fidelity — one more field in the project file plus its history.
fr5: A new card layout, a per-project chart and a per-project board: new component families beside Variant A.

fr1: The band answers “what needs me” first, with the action; the live rail adds eleven moving entries to the first screen.
fr2: Drill-in is the Claude sidebar literally: project → track → chats, one click to the chat.
fr3: The band keeps both needs-you tracks above the fold at 10 projects (the only variant that does), but the rail and chat leaves grow with every session (3.5 screens).
fr4: Its core structures (rail, leaves, Who-moves-next) depend on the session ↔ track join that covers 18 % of KPI rows today.
fr5: Needs live session liveness from claude-hub polled into Vibe Tracks plus three new surfaces.
